Code transitions and sensitivity

Source: vignettes/articles/code-transitions.Rmd
code-transitions.Rmd

Audit code frequencies

nis_audit_code_transition() summarizes named code groups by period. The example is a small invented data frame; use separate calls for ICD-9 and ICD-10 because the function matches only one code system at a time.

toy <- data.frame(
  YEAR = rep(2018:2020, each = 2),
  I10_DX1 = c("I5022", "E119", "I509", "E119", "I5022", "E119"),
  DISCWT = rep(1, 6)
)
nis_audit_code_transition(
  toy,
  codes = c(heart_failure = "I50", diabetes = "E11"),
  type = "dx"
)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    YEAR code_group   n_cohort_unweighted n_unweighted n_weighted pct_within_year
#>   <int> <chr>                      <int>        <int>      <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1  2018 heart_failu…                   2            1          1              50
#> 2  2019 heart_failu…                   2            1          1              50
#> 3  2020 heart_failu…                   2            1          1              50
#> 4  2018 diabetes                       2            1          1              50
#> 5  2019 diabetes                       2            1          1              50
#> 6  2020 diabetes                       2            1          1              50
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: yoy_pct_change <dbl>

The output gives unweighted and weighted group counts and each group’s share of all discharges within the period. A year-over-year percentage change is relative to the prior observed period; it is descriptive and does not explain why coding prevalence changed.

Compare diagnosis positions

Principal and secondary diagnoses can capture different presentations. nis_dx_sensitivity() compares counts and selected outcome rates across principal, secondary-only, and any-position definitions.

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019))
nis_dx_sensitivity(nis, "I50")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 9
#>   presentation n_unweighted n_weighted pct_of_any_unweighted pct_of_any_weighted
#>   <chr>               <dbl>      <dbl>                 <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1 principal              54       62.4                   100                 100
#> 2 secondary_o…            0        0                       0                   0
#> 3 any                    54       62.4                   100                 100
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: DIED_rate_unweighted <dbl>, DIED_rate_weighted <dbl>,
#> #   ELECTIVE_rate_unweighted <dbl>, ELECTIVE_rate_weighted <dbl>

The rows show how the synthetic definition changes with diagnosis position. These are descriptive weighted summaries, not survey estimates with standard errors. Use a survey design for inferential comparisons.

Handle the ICD transition

NIS changed from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM/PCS in October 2015. 2015 combines ICD-9 discharges from Q1–Q3 with ICD-10 discharges from Q4. Flag the systems separately using the appropriate slot names and version information; easyNIS does not supply a crosswalk or clinical equivalence decisions. ICD-9 helpers and code-system boundary checks are experimental.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • A trend break can reflect code-set changes, case mix, or practice as well as a true change in prevalence.
  • A zero in an audit means no match in the selected system, not absence in a different code system.
  • Principal and any-position summaries are nested definitions, not independent groups.

See nis_audit_code_transition(), nis_dx_sensitivity(), and nis_flag_dx_position().
